Heard learned counsel, Mr. Rath for the Petitioner and learned Standing Counsel, Mr.
Praharaj for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with Special G.R. Case No.18 of 2016, pending in the Court of learned Ad hoc Addl. District & Sessions Judge, FTSC (POCSO), Jagatsinghpur, arising out of Tirtol P.S. Case No.252 of 2016, for alleged commission of offence under Sections 376(2)(i)/376(D)/506/34 IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and Section 5/6 of the Odisha Prevention of Witch Hunting Act.

sentences.text:
3. Being aggrieved by the order dated 18.05.2023 passed by the learned Ad hoc Addl. District &
Sessions Judge, FTSC (POCSO), Jagatsinghpur, rejecting the prayer of the petitioner for regular/interim bail, the present bail application has been filed.

entities.text:
Ad hoc Addl. District &
Sessions Judge, FTSC (POCSO), Jagatsinghpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 27.07.2016.
5.
It is further submitted that the Petitioner had earlier approached this Court in BLAPL No.2167 of 2020 which was disposed of as withdrawn by order dated 1.7.2020.

Thereafter the Petitioner approached this Court unsuccessfully in BLAPL No.4229 of 2023 and the same was disposed of on 15.05.2023 and renewed his prayer unsuccessfully in BLAPL No.12148 of 2022 which was disposed of on 16.02.2023.

While doing so, this Court took note of the fact that out of 34 cited witnesses, 32 have been examined by 17.10.2022 and taking into account the nature of allegation and the role ascribed to the present Petitioner, this Court while not entertaining the bail application as noted Sipun @ Pravat Mallick vs State Of Odisha

sentences.text:
.... Opposite Party on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183152520/
1 gave liberty to the Petitioner to renew his prayer, if the trial is not concluded by end of March, 2023.

Since the trial is not concluded within such time frame, this is the 4th journey of the Petitioner to this Court.
6.

Perused the order passed by the learned Court in seisin dated 4.4.2023 in which while taking note of the order of this Court to conclude the trial by end of March, 2023 it is stated that the prosecution case is closed and the statement of the accused has been recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C on 15.02.2023.
Thereafter the case was posted to 10.03.2023 and 17.03.2023 to adduce defence evidence.

7. On 17.03.2023 the co-accused- Maina Baba @ Akhaya Kumar Naik, according to the learned counsel for the Petitioner who is the principal accused filed a petition to issue process to 3 witnesses named in the order as defence witnesses.

Accordingly, summons were issued to the said witnesses and the case was fixed to 11.04.2023.
8.

It is brought to the notice of this Court that the said co- accused approached this Court by filing CRLMC No.151 of 2023 and this Court by order dated 19.01.2023 issued notice to the Informant.
And

, in I.A. No.117 of 2023 passed therein directed that "as an interim measure, this Court directs that the learned court below shall continue with the trial in connection with Special G.R. Case No.18 of 2016 corresponding to Tirtol P.S. Case No.252 of 2016 but shall not conclude it without the leave of this Court".
9.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner, referring to the order passed by the learned Court in seisin dated 18.05.2023, that in obedience to the direction issued by this Court the case was posted to 6.6.2023 for argument subject to the order passed by this Court.
10. Learned counsel for the State submits that steps in right earnest have been taken in CRLMC No.151 of 2023 for modification/vacation of the interim order adverted to hereinabove.

11. Be that as it may, it is seen that the present Petitioner is in custody since 27.07.2016 and the trial is lingering at the instance of the co-accused and balancing the right of the accused vis--vis the victim, this Court directs the Petitioner to be released on interim bail for a period of four weeks from the date of his release.
Learned Court in seisin shall fix the terms.

12. Additionally, it is directed that during currency of the interim bail period, the Petitioner shall appear once a week before the jurisdictional police station on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin and shall also appear on each date of trial during such interim bail period.
13. It is needless to state that the Petitioner shall surrender on expiry of the interim bail period.

14. Call this matter on 26.09.2023.
15.
The CRLMC No.151 of 2023 called for reference be de- tagged from this BLAPL.
